title: Title verification before buying property - what lawyers actually check
p1:
A property can look perfect on paper and still hide a problem you never saw coming.

Before buying, many people only check the price, location, and builder reputation. But the biggest question is often: does the seller actually have a clean right to sell?
p2:
A common misconception is that a registered sale deed automatically means the property is safe. It doesn't.

Lawyers usually go deeper — they trace past ownership records, check whether previous transfers were valid, look for unpaid claims, disputes, restrictions, or anyone else who may have a legal interest in the property.
p3:
Title verification is basically a background check of the property's history. A lawyer is not just checking documents; they are checking whether those documents create a clear chain of ownership.

One missing link in that chain can create years of trouble after purchase. A small verification step before buying can protect a lifetime of savings.

Always ask for a proper title check before signing the final deal.
conclusion: Have you or someone you know ever faced a property issue because ownership documents were not properly verified? What would you check before buying your next property?
